_real_world.class: Northrop Grumman AN/APG-81 AESA fire-control radar
_real_world.variant_scope: AN/APG-81 as fitted to F-35C Lightning II (optional CVW-8 branch, count 0 in the 2025-26 deployment)
public_equipment: AN/APG-81 AESA, >150 km class detection range against a 1 sq m RCS target (Wikipedia/Deagel public spec)

_provenance.modeling_note: F-35C is the optional CVW-8 branch (count 0 in the 2025-26 baseline). The repo's F-35C reuse (eq-us-air-f35c) does not carry a radar record; this module supplies it. max_range is web-sourced (Wikipedia cites >150 km/93 mi against a non-stealth target; Deagel gives 150 km against 1 sq m RCS). Scan/track/noise parameters have no public figures and are proxy values patterned on CSG_US_APG-79 (aircraft/modules/sensors/csg/us/apg_79.json), nudged modestly better to reflect the APG-81's newer AESA generation and F-35 sensor-fusion role per Northrop Grumman's qualitative marketing claims, without asserting a specific quantified advantage.

sensor.max_range.note: 150 km class detection range (Wikipedia states >150 km with a citation-needed flag; Deagel gives 150 km against 1 sq m RCS); no Tier A/B figure found in 2 searches

sensor.fov_deg.note: proxy copied from CSG_US_APG-79, same AESA class; no public figure

sensor.scan_period.note: engineering_estimate marginally faster than CSG_US_APG-79's 1.0 s, reflecting the APG-81's newer AESA generation per Northrop Grumman marketing material; not a quantified figure

sensor.detection_prob.note: engineering_estimate marginally above CSG_US_APG-79's 0.92, same reasoning

sensor.range_power.note: proxy copied from CSG_US_APG-79 (radar-equation exponent, not platform-specific)

sensor.aspect_influence.note: engineering_estimate marginally below CSG_US_APG-79's 0.25, reflecting the F-35's low-observable-aware sensor-fusion design intent; not a quantified figure
